John Studholme Brownrigg | spouse = {{marriage|Elizabeth Rebecca Cassamaijor|11 December 1812}} | children = 3 | relations = [[Robert Brownrigg]] (uncle) }} '''John Studholme Brownrigg''' (17 March 1786{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ve8_AQAAMAAJ&pg=PA182|title=Burke's Genealogical and Heraldic History of the Peerage, Baronetage and Knightage|year=1885|page=182}} – 1853){{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XZjajWFP4OYC&pg=PA227 |title=The Gladstone Diaries: 1825-1832 : 1833-1839 |page=227 |last=Gladstone |first=William Ewart |isbn=0198213700 |year=1969|publisher=Oxford University Press }} was an English merchant and British [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] politician who sat in the [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|House of Commons]] from 1835 to 1847. ==Early life== Brownrigg was born on 17 March 1786 in Windsor. He was the third son of Lydia ({{nee}} Eames) Brownrigg, of [[Boston, Massachusetts]], and Lt. John Studholme Brownrigg (1754–1787) of the 38th Foot. His paternal uncle was [[Sir Robert Brownrigg, 1st Baronet]], the [[Governor of British Ceylon]]. ==Career== An [[East India Company]] military cadet of the 1800 season, he arrived in India in August 1801 and was commissioned [[ensign (rank)|ensign]] in the 12th [[Bengal Native Infantry]] in November 1801, being promoted to Lieutenant in September 1803. He served under General Lake with the 12th N.I. in the [[Second Mahratta War]], being present at the [[Battle of Laswarree]], on 1 November 1803, "as fierce a fight as was ever fought by men." In 1851, he received the [[Army of India Medal]] with clasp for Laswarree. Brownrigg transferred to the 8th N.I., and was Adjutant and Quartermaster of that unit between 1805 and 1810. He served in the capture of Java in August 1811 but neither claimed nor received the medal for that campaign. He was also Secretary to the Military Board from February 1813 until his resignation from the army in April 1820, having been promoted Captain in February 1815. After his HEIC army service, Brownrigg became a [[London]] merchant and partner in [[Sir Charles Cockerell, 1st Baronet|Charles Cockerill]] & Co.{{cite web |title=John Studholme Brownrigg {{!}} Legacies of British Slavery |url=http://wwwdepts-live.ucl.ac.uk/lbs/person/view/2146006976 |website=wwwdepts-live.ucl.ac.uk |publisher=UCL Department of History |access-date=5 January 2023}} He was also a director of the [[Australia and New Zealand Banking Group|Royal Bank of Australasia]] and deputy governor of the [[Australian Agricultural Company]].{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=I1MNAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA153 |title=Dod's Parliamentary Companion |page=153 |volume=15 |year=1847 |last=Dod |first=Charles Roger |author2=Dod, Robert Phipps}} Captain Brownrigg was an unsuccessful candidate for the [[Boston (UK Parliament constituency)|borough of Boston]] in the [[1832 United Kingdom general election|1832 general election]] but was elected in the [[1835 United Kingdom general election|1835 election]] and re-elected in the [[1837 United Kingdom general election|1837]] and [[1841 United Kingdom general election|1841 election]]s.{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/details/historyandantiq00thomgoog |title=The History and Antiquities of Boston: And the Villages of Skirbeck, Fishtoft, Freiston, Butterwick, Benington, Leverton, Leake, and Wrangle; Comprising the Hundred of Skirbeck, in the County of Lincoln |publisher=Longman |page=[https://archive.org/details/historyandantiq00thomgoog/page/n505 453] |year=1856 |last=Thompson |first=Pishey}} Captain Brownrigg represented Boston as a Member of Parliament until his retirement in 1847.{{cite book |last1=Thompson |first1=Pishey |title=The History and Antiquities of Boston: And the Villages of Skirbeck, Fishtoft, Freiston, Butterwick, Benington, Leverton, Leake, and Wrangle; Comprising the Hundred of Skirbeck, in the County of Lincoln |date=1856 |publisher=J. Noble |page=453 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=x8w-AAAAcAAJ&pg=PA453 |access-date=5 January 2023 |language=en}} ==Personal life== On 11 December 1812, he married Elizabeth Rebecca Cassamaijor, a daughter of James Henry Cassamaijor, Esq. Together, they were the parents of:{{cite book |title=Genealogical and Heraldic Dictionary of the Peerage and Baronetage of the British Empire |date=1898 |publisher=Burke's Peerage Limited. |page=207 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NlhQAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA207 |access-date=5 January 2023 |language=en}} * John Studholme Brownrigg (1814–1889), a General who fought in the [[Crimean War]]; he married Katharine Williams-Wynn, daughter of Sir [[Henry Williams-Wynn]], in 1840. After her death, he married Beatrice Laura Desanges, daughter of [[Louis William Desanges]].{{cite book |title=Debrett's Peerage, Baronetage, Knightage, and Companionage |date=1916 |publisher=Kelly's Directories |page=82 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ujg4TVs_3RkC&pg=PA82 |access-date=5 January 2023 |language=en}} * Sophia Ann Brownrigg (1816–1906), who married Sir [[Charles Alexander Wood]], son of [[Thomas Wood (1777–1860)|Thomas Wood]], MP for [[Breconshire (UK Parliament constituency)|Breconshire]] and [[aide-de-camp]] to [[Queen Victoria]], in 1838. * Jane Agnes Brownrigg (1818–1891), who married [[Sir John Harington, 10th Baronet]], son of [[Harington baronets|Sir James Harington, 9th Baronet]], in 1846. He died at home in Middlesex in September 1853.See DNW auction of 13 September 2012 for detail on military biography. == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == * {{Hansard-contribs | mr-john-brownrigg | John Studholme Brownrigg}} {{s-start}} {{s-par|uk}} {{s-bef | before = [[John Wilks (MP)|John Wilks]] | before2 = [[Benjamin Handley]] }} {{s-ttl | title = [[Member of Parliament]] for [[Boston (UK Parliament constituency)|Boston]] | years = [[1835 United Kingdom general election|1835]]–[[1847 United Kingdom general election|1847]] | with = [[John Wilks (MP)|John Wilks]] 1835–37 | with2 = [[Sir James Duke, 1st Baronet|Sir James Duke]] 1837–49 }} {{s-aft | after = [[Sir James Duke, 1st Baronet|Sir James Duke]] | after2 = [[Benjamin Bond Cabbell]] }} {{s-end}} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Brownrigg, John Studholme}} [[Category:1786 births]] [[Category:1853 deaths]] [[Category:Conservative Party (UK) MPs for English constituencies]] [[Category:Members of the Parliament of the United Kingdom for English constituencies]] [[Category:UK MPs 1835–1837]] [[Category:UK MPs 1837–1841]] [[Category:UK MPs 1841–1847]] [[Category:19th-century British merchants]]
